findings.claim: MCQ: 'Which one of the following is found in a bacterial cell but NOT in an animal cell? A) Mitochondria B) Cell membrane C) Nucleus D) Chloroplasts' - answer key 'B) Cell membrane'.
findings.truth: Animal cells have a cell membrane, so option B does not answer the stem, and no listed option did. Option B changed to 'Plasmids', which are found only in prokaryotic cells; the note in the mark scheme even contradicted its own key by stating that animal cells have a cell membrane.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1b (plasmids listed for prokaryotic cells only); settled fact

findings.claim: A mitochondrion 0.2 um (200 nm) long: 'This is just within the resolution limit of an electron microscope.'
findings.truth: 200 nm is about 1000 times coarser than the electron microscope limit of about 0.2 nm, which the same lesson states twice. 200 nm is the light microscope limit.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1c (increased resolution in a transmission electron microscope); the lesson's own figures

findings.claim: 'embryonic stem cells are totipotent'
findings.truth: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent. The body text and practice question 4 of the same lesson both say pluripotent, so the takeaway contradicts the lesson.
findings.evidence: settled fact; internal contradiction with content_html n23 and practice_questions[3]

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Investigating Enzyme Activity (PAG B3)'
findings.truth: PAG B3 is Sampling techniques. Rates of enzyme-controlled reactions is PAG B4.
findings.evidence: spec Topic B7 PAG table; spec B1.2f and B1.2g practical suggestions tagged (PAG B2, PAG B4, PAG B6)

findings.claim: 6-mark question 'Describe the role of DNA in protein synthesis...' with mRNA, transcription and the triplet code in the mark scheme, carrying no tier flag.
findings.truth: B1.2d and B1.2e are bold, so they are tested only on the Higher Tier papers. The lesson already hides the matching content in a higher-only wrapper, so a Foundation student meets the question but not the teaching.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B1.2d, B1.2e

findings.claim: Flashcard 'What is the triplet code in DNA?' with no tier flag.
findings.truth: The triplet code is bold statement B1.2e, Higher Tier only.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B1.2e

findings.claim: Takeaway: 'Its base sequence (triplet code) determines the order of amino acids in proteins.'
findings.truth: The triplet code is Higher Tier only (B1.2e) and the lesson hides it in a higher-only wrapper, but the takeaway named it unflagged. The sentence stays true without the term.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B1.2e

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Investigating Respiration (PAG B3)'
findings.truth: PAG B3 is Sampling techniques. PAG B6 is Physiology, responses and respiration.
findings.evidence: spec Topic B7 PAG table; spec B1.3c practical suggestions tagged (PAG B2, PAG B4, PAG B5, PAG B6)

findings.claim: The inverse square law is taught and assessed with no tier flag: a whole worked-example collapsible, a sentence in the limiting-factors paragraph, the key fact, the takeaway, practice question 5, knowledge check 2 and flashcard 3.
findings.truth: BM1.4v ('understand and use inverse proportion - the inverse square law and light intensity in the context of factors affecting photosynthesis') is bold, so Higher Tier only. The worked example is now wrapped in higher-only and the four assessment items are tagged. B1.4f (interaction of limiting factors) was already correctly wrapped.
findings.evidence: spec bold file BM1.4v, B1.4f

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Investigating Osmosis (PAG B4)'
findings.truth: PAG B4 is Rates of enzyme-controlled reactions. PAG B8 is Transport in and out of cells, and its named example activity is the potato chip water potential investigation.
findings.evidence: spec Topic B7 PAG table; spec B2.1a practical suggestions tagged (PAG B6, PAG B8)

findings.claim: Osmosis flashcard answer ends '...through a partially permeable.'
findings.truth: The noun was missing. It should read 'through a partially permeable membrane.' The lesson's own exam tip tells students to use that exact term.
findings.evidence: spec B2.1a; the lesson's glossary entry for osmosis

findings.claim: A section 'The Digestive System' (stomach, protease, pancreas, large intestine, liver, bile, emulsification, lipase) and a collapsible 'Villi - Adaptations for Absorption'.
findings.truth: None of this is in J247. The words digest, villi, bile, lipase, protease and stomach appear nowhere in the specification. It reads as AQA digestion content. The alveoli material is defensible under B2.2a and B2.2c as an exchange surface example, but the digestion detail is off-spec revision time. Options: cut the digestion section at the next content pass and keep villi only as a second exchange-surface example, or leave it as enrichment and label it as beyond the specification. A cut would delete narration blocks n23 to n26, so it is not a surgical edit.
findings.evidence: grep of specs/ocr/biology-a-gateway-J247.md: zero hits for digest, villi, bile, lipase, protease, stomach

findings.claim: The 'Blood Components' collapsible teaches white blood cells (phagocytes, lymphocytes) and platelets.
findings.truth: B2.2e covers red blood cells and plasma only. White blood cells and platelets are B6.3, which sits on Paper 2. Harmless as background, and B1 to B3 is assumed knowledge in Paper 2 anyway.
findings.evidence: spec B2.2e; spec B6.3 'explain how white blood cells and platelets are adapted to their defence functions in the blood'

findings.claim: 'Three regions are particularly important to know (B3.1d):' introducing the brain.
findings.truth: B3.1d is the eye. The brain is B3.1f.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1d 'explain how the main structures of the eye are related to their functions'; B3.1f 'describe the structure and function of the brain'

findings.claim: The lesson teaches three brain parts: cerebral cortex, cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
findings.truth: B3.1f names five parts and is assessed at both tiers: cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla, hypothalamus and pituitary. The hypothalamus was taught nowhere in the unit. The n17 sentence now names all five, n18 uses the spec term cerebrum, and n20 gains the hypothalamus and the pituitary.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.1f 'cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla, hypothalamus, pituitary' (not bold, so both tiers)

findings.claim: Question 4 and its mark scheme contain KaTeX markup, e.g. '\\(t = \\sqrt{\\frac{2d}{g}}\\)' and '\\(\\frac{0.24}{9.8} = 0.02449\\)'.
findings.truth: Practice question text renders as plain text, so the student saw raw backslash code instead of an equation. Rewritten with unicode: t = √(2d ÷ g), g = 9.8 m/s². The arithmetic itself is right: 0.24 / 9.8 = 0.024489..., square root = 0.1565 s, 0.16 s to 2 s.f.
findings.evidence: recomputation; practice.html renders question text as textContent

findings.claim: Eye defects cover short-sightedness and long-sightedness only.
findings.truth: B3.1e also names colour blindness, and it is assessed at both tiers. Adding it would need a new sentence in the vision-defects paragraph at the next content pass.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1e 'colour blindness, short-sightedness and long-sightedness'

findings.claim: 'Hormones can also be used to help people who have difficulty conceiving (B3.2e, Higher Tier).'
findings.truth: B3.2e is contraception. Fertility treatment is B3.2f, which is bold, so the Higher Tier claim is right but the code is wrong.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2f 'explain the use of hormones in modern reproductive technologies to treat infertility'

findings.claim: Plant hormones introduced as 'auxin and gibberellin (B3.2e)'.
findings.truth: B3.2e is contraception. Plant hormones are B3.2g (auxins, phototropisms and gravitropisms) and B3.2h (auxins, plus gibberellins and ethene in bold).
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2g, B3.2h

findings.claim: Only phototropism is taught. Gravitropism appears nowhere in the unit.
findings.truth: B3.2g requires 'the role of auxins in phototropisms and gravitropisms' and is not bold, so it is assessed at both tiers. Two sentences added to the auxin paragraph: auxin gathers on the lower side of a root and slows growth there so the root bends down; in a shoot the same uneven spread speeds growth so the shoot bends up.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2g

findings.claim: Takeaway lists rooting powders, selective weedkillers, ethene fruit ripening and gibberellin germination with no tier flag.
findings.truth: B3.2i is bold in full, and the gibberellin, ethene, germination and fruit-ripening parts of B3.2h are bold. The lesson already hides the matching body content in a higher-only wrapper, so the unflagged takeaway contradicted it.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2h, B3.2i

findings.claim: Practice question 5 (commercial gibberellin), practice question 6 (fertility treatments), knowledge check 5 (plant hormone uses) and flashcards 5, 6 and 7 test statements the lesson hides from Foundation students.
findings.truth: All rest on bold statements B3.2f, B3.2h (gibberellins and ethene) and B3.2i. Each now carries a Higher tier tag.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2f, B3.2h, B3.2i

findings.claim: The higher-only wrapper around n9 hides the whole four-hormone paragraph of the menstrual cycle.
findings.truth: The paragraph mixes tiers. The roles of oestrogen, progesterone and FSH are B3.2c, which is not bold and is assessed at both tiers; only the feedback interactions of FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone are bold B3.2d. The paragraph is one narration block, so it cannot be split without changing the block count. Recommendation: keep the wrapper, because the unwrapped key fact n10 and the exam tip already give Foundation students each hormone's role. Related: LH itself appears only inside bold B3.2d, yet the unwrapped key fact, takeaway, exam tip, knowledge check 1 and flashcard 2 all teach and test it. Testosterone (B3.2c, both tiers) is taught nowhere in the unit.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B3.2c (not bold, 'oestrogen, progesterone, FSH and testosterone'), B3.2d (bold, 'FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone')

findings.claim: The unit maps 8 lessons to Paper 1 and covers B1.1 to B3.2 only. Sub-topic B3.3 'Maintaining internal environments' is absent.
findings.truth: B3.3 is a Topic B3 sub-topic, so the spec places it on Paper 1 (Foundation) and Paper 3 (Higher). Its two lessons exist but sit in the biology-paper-2 unit as lessons 1 and 2: 'Homeostasis, Blood Glucose and Temperature' and 'The Kidneys and Osmoregulation'. Paper 2 and Paper 4 assess B4 to B6, with B1 to B3 only as assumed knowledge. A student revising for Paper 1 therefore skips homeostasis, insulin and glucagon, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, kidney structure and ADH. Recommendation: move those two lessons into biology-paper-1 as lessons 9 and 10 and renumber the Paper 2 unit. That change ripples through lesson numbering, narration order and podcasts, so it needs Tom's word.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a: 'Paper 1 assesses content from Topics B1-B3 and B7'; 'Paper 2 assesses content from Topics B4-B6 and B7, with assumed knowledge of Topics B1-B3'; spec B3.3a to B3.3j; scripts/_content_separate-sciences-ocr/lessons/*.json _unit_slug values

findings.claim: Board anchors checked across all 8 lessons.
findings.truth: No wrong exam claims found. No lesson states a paper count, duration, mark total or tier structure, so there is nothing that contradicts 4 papers of 1 hour 45 minutes and 90 marks at 50 per cent each. Practicals are named as PAGs throughout, never as required or core practicals. No banned rubric phrase, band name or spec code appears; the 'Award 1 mark each for' and 'Award up to 3 marks:' forms do not match the validator pattern. The highest tariff used is 6 marks, which matches the single extended-response question. All 24 knowledge check answer keys and all match orders were recomputed and are correct, as were every magnification, percentage change, surface area to volume, rate and inverse square law worked example.
findings.evidence: spec sections 2a and 3a; recomputation

summary: 8 lessons checked against OCR Gateway Biology A J247. 25 findings: 2 HIGH (an MCQ with no correct option, and raw KaTeX rendered as plain text in a practice question and its mark scheme), 20 MEDIUM, 3 LOW. 34 surgical edits. The dominant faults are tier flagging against the bold spec (the inverse square law, the triplet code and the commercial plant hormone statements were taught or tested with no Higher tier flag) and wrong references: three of the four PAG citations named the wrong Practical Activity Group, and three spec codes were wrong. Every calculation and every answer key recomputed correct. Unit level: sub-topic B3.3 is missing from this Paper 1 unit because its two lessons sit in the biology-paper-2 unit, and Lesson 6 teaches a digestive system section that is nowhere in J247.
